pairs.subject: prompt-safety
pairs.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_prompt_fences.py:308 The JSON-fence binding test only feeds a payload that never tries to close its fence; fenced_untrusted passes a forged <<<END_UNTRUSTED_TAG>>> through verbatim inside the JSON string (verified: the close marker appears twice), so the scorecard transcript and group-compare fences are forgeable and no test catches it.

techniques.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_prompt_fences.py:308 Prose fences are defused and non-vacuity-tested well, but the JSON fences (fixed marker, no nonce, no stripping) are only tested with a marker-free payload; the line-297 rationale that json.dumps escapes the needed newlines is wrong, since a model does not need a newline to read a closing marker.

pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_credentials.py:105 An unreadable CV skips the check that corroborates a model-listed licence, and the test pins the same empty list a clean check returns; there is no not-inspected outcome.
pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_prompt_budgets.py:39 Per-block caps (JD, company, CV, summary, highlight, label, verdict) cut with a visible marker; in-budget text stays byte-identical.
pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_automation.py:947 Model-emitted scorecard entities are type-checked and non-conforming members dropped rather than trusted.
pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_automation_constant_sync.py:52 The transcript budget cap is single-sourced in Python, generated into TS, and pinned by a test on both sides.

pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_claude_cli.py:148 Generate mode runs in an empty cwd; repo access only through with_repo_access's read-only door; the API key is stripped from the spawn env (line 261). The roster is cut at design time.

pairs.registryProposal: untrusted-span-fencing should name JSON-encoding as a non-fence: json.dumps escapes quotes and newlines but leaves fixed angle-bracket markers intact, so a 'JSON fence' with a fixed close tag still needs stripping or a nonce; teams treat the encoding as the neutralization.

pairs.subject: prompt-safety
pairs.evidence: scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:328 guardPlan maps any action other than 'delete' (a misspelt or invented verb) onto a whole-file write instead of rejecting it, which is the 'fuzzily matched to the nearest legal operation' failure of a closed grammar.

techniques.evidence: scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:328 Paths, the protected prefixes, sizes and the commit subject are validated well; the verb set is not closed.

scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:426 The fence is always longer than any backtick run in the payload (stripping-class unforgeability), with the UNTRUSTED_TASK_LABEL provenance label in both rounds; pinned by injection.test.

scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:269 Source reads are capped per file and per count with a visible marker, and the meter checks the token budget before each call. The issue-body task text has no class cap of its own beyond GitHub's limit.
scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:544 Model-authored summary, verification and risks go into the proposal markdown posted to the tracker with no secret masking or @mention/link neutralization.

scripts/agent/__tests__/injection.test.mjs:20 Assumes the injection fully worked and asserts guardPlan denies the win (protected gates, .env, test deletions, traversal); the output is a draft PR gated like any change.

scripts/security/secret-scan.mjs:242 The blocking secret gate skips tracked files over 2 MB (printed as 'not read') and still exits 0; a committer can pad a file past the window. Binary-extension and unreadable files are skipped and not counted at all.
